verdict.reasoning: The patient reports feeling under the weather for four days with symptoms starting with a sore throat and runny nose, now progressing to a dry cough and fatigue.
The patient mentions the onset of symptoms after a colleague was sneezing next to him, suggesting workplace exposure.
The patient states the sore throat was painful for one or two days and is now improving.
The patient describes the runny nose as clearing up and now experiencing nasal congestion.
The patient reports a dry, constant cough that started recently, specifically mentioning it began yesterday.
The patient explicitly mentions experiencing night sweats.
The patient had an initial fever that is improving with the use of paracetamol and ibuprofen.
The patient experiences dyspnea on exertion but no shortness of breath at rest and no chest pain.
The patient reports intermittent, generalized headaches with no vision changes or photophobia.
The patient denies nausea or vomiting and reports normal bowel and urinary function.
The patient mentions a slightly reduced appetite and increased fluid intake.
The patient reports myalgias that started in the past couple of days.
The patient denies ear pain, discharge, and rash.
The patient states he is otherwise fit and well with no other medical problems.
The patient uses paracetamol for fever.
The patient uses ibuprofen as needed for fever.
The patient denies any allergies, including drug allergies.
The patient mentions his grandmother has type 2 diabetes.
The patient mentions a great-grandfather had eczema.
The patient lives alone and works as an accountant.
The patient is working but slower due to stress, which he describes as good work stress.
The patient occasionally uses cigars at work events and has low social alcohol use.
The doctor summarizes the symptoms as a viral URI or early influenza, noting workplace exposure.
The patient experiences dyspnea on exertion in the context of a viral illness, without rest SOB or chest pain.
The doctor associates night sweats with the acute viral syndrome.
The doctor recommends supportive care, including rest and increased oral fluids.
The doctor advises continuing paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed for antipyretic and analgesic effects.
The doctor suggests considering taking 1-2 days off work and resuming activities as tolerated.

The doctor advises returning or going to the emergency department if experiencing high or persistent fever, worsening cough or SOB, chest pain, inability to maintain hydration, or if not improving by next week.
The doctor advises returning to the clinic for reassessment if not better next week.
